To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
[11C]-UCB-J PET in mice showed a high specificity to SV2A and that 1TCM with IDIF is an optimal model for quantification of [11C]-UBC-J in mouse brain.
[11C]-UCB-J PET is a promising tool to quantify synaptic density in mice.
we validated [11C] UCB-J in mice as a PET radiotracer for the quantification of synaptic density.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and evaluation of new radiolabeled compounds for the imaging of the brain with positron emission tomograph (PET).
the development of a novel PET tracer, [11C]UBC-J, which is a selective radioligand for synaptic vesicle glycolipid 2A (sv2A), a marker of presynaptic function.
the development of a radioligand for PET imaging of the synaptic vesicle glycosylated protein SV2A, which plays an important role in the regulation of neurotransmitter release.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the [11C] UCJ-J PET radiotracer has been successfully validated in mice and can now be used to measure synaptic density in comparative and therapeutic studies in mouse models of neuropsychiatric and neurological disorders.
the [11C] UCB-J radioligand is a promising radiotracer for noninvasive quantification of SV2A in mice.

the radioligands [11C]AB928 and [11C]PBR28 have similar properties, but [11C] AB928 is a more specific radioligand. [11C] PBR28 has a higher affinity for the PBR and is therefore a more suitable radioligand for the study of the PBR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have validated and characterized [11C]UB-J in mice.
the [11C] UCB-J radiotracer is a promising tool for non-invasive measurement of SV2A density and thus synaptic function.
[11C]-UCB-J is a suitable radiotracer to study synaptic density in the mouse.
The main takeaway from our work is that
[11C]-UCB-J is a promising radiotracer to noninvasivelly measure synaptic alterations in mice.
[11C]-UCB-J is an excellent radiotracer for imaging of SV2A in mouse brain, and that the radiotracer has a very rapid metabolism.
[11C]-UCB-J can be used to measure the synaptic density in mice.
